surprises.head: Vegas brought the hits
surprises.body: Vegas usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 179 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 87 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for Carter Hart
surprises.body: Hart allowed 6 goals on 21 shots, worth 3.0 expected goals: 3.0 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 35 starts.

story.head: Kucherov ties Stamkos for the Lightning’s points record
paras: The first period was a wild one. Brandon Hagel opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play early in the period, but Ivan Barbashev tied it 1-1 for Vegas midway through the period. John Carlson restored the Lightning’s lead 48 seconds later. Mark Stone tied it 2-2 for Vegas shorthanded four and a half minutes later, but that was the last goal the Golden Knights would get. Anthony Cirelli scored early in the second and again three and a half minutes later to put the Lightning up 4-2. Victor Hedman stretched the lead to 5-2 late in the period, and Nikita Kucherov made it 6-2 early in the third. Kucherov finished with a goal and two assists.

The Golden Knights outshot the Lightning 34-21, but the Lightning’s looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Vasilevskiy shook off a shaky start for the Bolts, allowing two goals on the first ten shots and none on the last 24, and Carter Hart allowed six goals on 21 shots.
The Lightning killed all four Golden Knights power plays. The Lightning moved to 7-2-0, second in the Atlantic, while the Golden Knights dropped to 8-3-0, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: Nikita Kucherov tied Steven Stamkos for first on the Lightning’s all-time scoring list, with 1,137 points.
Mark Stone passed Reilly Smith for third on the Golden Knights’ all-time goals list, with 144.
The Golden Knights’ three-game winning streak is over.
Three straight wins for the Lightning.
